## Dev harness
Token-protected test RPC: POST /webhook/dev with { target, input }. Routes to a fixed sub-workflow by target and responds synchronously with that sub-workflow's own result, since the caller needs the result itself, not just an acknowledgment. raise-error always fails on purpose, to prove the error handler fires. An unmatched target answers 404.

parameters.query: WITH d AS (DELETE FROM inbound_messages WHERE starts_with(phone, $1) RETURNING 1) SELECT count(*)::int AS messages FROM d
WITH d AS (DELETE FROM n8n_chat_histories WHERE starts_with(session_id, 'test:' || $1) OR starts_with(session_id, $1) RETURNING 1) SELECT count(*)::int AS memories FROM d

## upsert-patient / find-patient
upsert-patient forwards straight to its sub-workflow. find-patient loads context, looks up the phone by exact match (Always Output Data, so no match still yields one empty item), drops that placeholder, and wraps whatever's left into { rows }, which is [] for a first-time patient.

## cleanup
A phone_prefix must match ^\d{8,}$ (digits only, 8+), or the request is refused with prefix_too_short before anything is deleted. Each of the four parts (Calendar events, Sheets rows, inbound_messages, n8n_chat_histories) continues on error, so one failing part doesn't block the others; a failed part reports null, and ok is true only when all four succeed. Calendar and Sheets match the prefix with a literal, case-sensitive startsWith/substring check in a Filter node, never a pattern built from the prefix, and the two Postgres deletes use starts_with($1), never LIKE, which a prefix like "________" would turn into a wildcard that deletes every row. Sheets rows are deleted one at a time by row_number descending, so a deletion can't shift the rows still queued. For Calendar and Sheets, a delete's success and error outputs both feed one Aggregate (Always Output Data, so zero matches counts as 0), tagged ok:true/ok:false, and count-cleanup-outcomes reduces it to one count, or null if any outcome failed, so exactly one item per part reaches the merge chain.
